text.p: Bonds (OT) were edging higher in thin trade with a slight out-performance compared with the Spanish Bonos attributable to a lack of paper in the local market, traders said.
The shorter end was seen as having more potential upside, taking advantage of a slight easing in money market rates and the steadiness of the escudo, they added.
"The OT are benefitting from the favourable winds blowing from Spain, where the market is betting on a good inflation number for February. This is giving support along the curve," said one trader.
"In the 10 years, the (negative) spreads widened with Spain and the (positive) spreads narrowed with the Bunds, but this is due to the lack of paper in this sector," said another trader.
The spread with the German equivalent narrowed to around 112 basis points from 117 on Tuesday.
For the futures, resistance was seen at 108.00, with intra-day support at 107.25/30.
